title.narrative: Immediate response with temporary shelter and basic living conditions, prioritizing people vulnerable, affected by Hurricane Rafael in critical municipalities of Artemisa and Mayabeque, Cuba

description.narrative: The project focuses on life-saving in time critical shelter criteria and non-food relief items (NRFI) for the immediate provision of temporary and semi-temporary emergency shelter for hurricane Rafael affected people in the worst hit municipalities of Artemisa and Mayabeque provinces (The provinces most affected by the hurricane). In these territories, over 22 000 houses were destroyed or severely damaged affecting more 88 000 people. (preliminarily, because the damage assessment is still ongoing). However, Cuba faces a total of more 37 100 damaged homes with more 129 500 affected people, considering the impact of Hurricane Rafael in the provinces of Artemisa, Mayabeque and Havana, as well as the earthquake in the eastern part of the country. Additionally, more than 90,000 people were recently affected by Hurricane Oscar. In total (in the housing sector alone, not considering severe damage to infrastructure), the country must assist more 307,500 affected people in less than a month.A rights-based approach will be used to promote an immediate and gender-sensitive response. Priority will be given to families with women and people in the most vulnerable situations. This includes women who are pregnant, have children and/or are caring for dependents. Also, women with limited socio-economic resources, women members of families living in situations of violence or victims of gender-based violence. People with disabilities, who are sick or in need of permanent care, as well as senior citizens will also be prioritized.
